pages.quiz:
ENGLISH — GENERAL ASSESSMENT #1
====

GRADE: Grade 8
SUBJECT: ENGLISH
TIME ALLOWED: 45 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 30
EXAM BODY: KJSEA

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show formula → substitution → steps → final answer with units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the best option.
4. Check your work before submitting.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. A noun is a word that names: (1 mark)
   A. Only an action
   B. Only a describing word
   C. A person, place, thing, or idea
   D. Only a joining word

2. When practising Listening and Speaking 1.1.1 Polite Language: Telephone Etiquette, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Listening and Speaking 1.1.1 Polite Language: Telephone Etiquette.
   B. Use insults to “practise” Listening and Speaking 1.1.1 Polite Language: Telephone Etiquette.
   C. Avoid reading anything related to Listening and Speaking 1.1.1 Polite Language: Telephone Etiquette.
   D. Copy random text without understanding Listening and Speaking 1.1.1 Polite Language: Telephone Etiquette.

3. A paragraph should usually have: (1 mark)
   A. Only one word repeated
   B. Many unrelated topics with no link
   C. One main idea with supporting sentences
   D. No full stops

4. When practising Listening and Speaking 2.1.1 Oral Presentations: Songs, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Copy random text without understanding Listening and Speaking 2.1.1 Oral Presentations: Songs.
   B. Use insults to “practise” Listening and Speaking 2.1.1 Oral Presentations: Songs.
   C. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Listening and Speaking 2.1.1 Oral Presentations: Songs.
   D. Avoid reading anything related to Listening and Speaking 2.1.1 Oral Presentations: Songs.

5. When practising : Stressed and unstressed words, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Use insults to “practise” : Stressed and unstressed words.
   B. Copy random text without understanding : Stressed and unstressed words.
   C. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for : Stressed and unstressed words.
   D. Avoid reading anything related to : Stressed and unstressed words.

6. Choose the correctly punctuated sentence. (1 mark)
   A. Where is the library?
   B. Where is the Library
   C. Where is the library
   D. where is the library

7. When practising Grammar in Use 15.3.1 Types of Sentences: Interrogative sentences, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Copy random text without understanding Grammar in Use 15.3.1 Types of Sentences: Interrogative sentences.
   B. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Grammar in Use 15.3.1 Types of Sentences: Interrogative sentences.
   C. Use insults to “practise” Grammar in Use 15.3.1 Types of Sentences: Interrogative sentences.
   D. Avoid reading anything related to Grammar in Use 15.3.1 Types of Sentences: Interrogative sentences.

8. When practising Writing 1.5.1 Writing legibly and neatly, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Use insults to “practise” Writing 1.5.1 Writing legibly and neatly.
   B. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Writing 1.5.1 Writing legibly and neatly.
   C. Copy random text without understanding Writing 1.5.1 Writing legibly and neatly.
   D. Avoid reading anything related to Writing 1.5.1 Writing legibly and neatly.

9. The past tense of “go” is: (1 mark)
   A. going
   B. went
   C. goes
   D. goed

10. Which word is a verb? (1 mark)
   A. blue
   B. quickly
   C. run
   D. happiness

11. When practising Grammar in Use 1.3.1 Word classes: Compound Nouns, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Avoid reading anything related to Grammar in Use 1.3.1 Word classes: Compound Nouns.
   B. Copy random text without understanding Grammar in Use 1.3.1 Word classes: Compound Nouns.
   C. Use insults to “practise” Grammar in Use 1.3.1 Word classes: Compound Nouns.
   D. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Grammar in Use 1.3.1 Word classes: Compound Nouns.

12. When practising Reading 1.4.1 Intensive Reading: Short Stories, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Reading 1.4.1 Intensive Reading: Short Stories.
   B. Copy random text without understanding Reading 1.4.1 Intensive Reading: Short Stories.
   C. Use insults to “practise” Reading 1.4.1 Intensive Reading: Short Stories.
   D. Avoid reading anything related to Reading 1.4.1 Intensive Reading: Short Stories.

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
13. In three clear sentences, explain Writing 7.5.1 Composition Writing and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

14. In three clear sentences, explain Listening and Speaking 8.1.1 Listening and Responding: Oral Narratives - Myths and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

15. In three clear sentences, explain Reading 8.2.1 Intensive Reading: Poem and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

16. In three clear sentences, explain Grammar in Use 8.3.1 Word Classes: Simple prepositions and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

MARKING SCHEME
====

1. C — A person, place, thing, or idea

2. A — Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Listening and Speaking 1.1.1 Polite Language: Telephone Etiquette.

3. C — One main idea with supporting sentences

4. C — Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Listening and Speaking 2.1.1 Oral Presentations: Songs.

5. C — Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for : Stressed and unstressed words.

6. A — Where is the library?

7. B — Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Grammar in Use 15.3.1 Types of Sentences: Interrogative sentences.

8. B — Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Writing 1.5.1 Writing legibly and neatly.

9. B — went

10. C — run

11. D — Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Grammar in Use 1.3.1 Word classes: Compound Nouns.

12. A — Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Reading 1.4.1 Intensive Reading: Short Stories.

13. (4 marks)
Award marks for: (1) accurate definition/idea of Writing 7.5.1 Composition Writing; (2) correct use of subject terms; (3) a relevant local example (home, school, market, farm, or community). Do not award for slogans with no content.

14. (4 marks)
Award marks for: (1) accurate definition/idea of Listening and Speaking 8.1.1 Listening and Responding: Oral Narratives - Myths; (2) correct use of subject terms; (3) a relevant local example (home, school, market, farm, or community). Do not award for slogans with no content.

15. (4 marks)
Award marks for: (1) accurate definition/idea of Reading 8.2.1 Intensive Reading: Poem; (2) correct use of subject terms; (3) a relevant local example (home, school, market, farm, or community). Do not award for slogans with no content.

16. (4 marks)
Award marks for: (1) accurate definition/idea of Grammar in Use 8.3.1 Word Classes: Simple prepositions; (2) correct use of subject terms; (3) a relevant local example (home, school, market, farm, or community). Do not award for slogans with no content.
